rubrics.criterion: The DNS update flow consumes a domain as one value again: the periodic per-domain update loop entry, the one-shot update entry, and the DNS record-update step each accept a single domain record value (the configuration model's domain-entry type, or an equivalent record grouping the domain's name, subdomain list, and provider) instead of re-declaring those three fields as individually typed parameters.
rubrics.rationale: This instance's core smell is the decomposed domain record recurring through the update-flow signatures in two production files; restoring one record value through loop, one-shot, and record-update step is the central semantic outcome of the task.

rubrics.criterion: Per-domain provider resolution inside the update flow works from the domain record, and the answer to 'which provider handles this domain' lives in one place: the domain's own provider when it names one, otherwise the configured global provider, with the multi-provider map and legacy single-provider paths behaving as before.
rubrics.rationale: The injected state re-answers 'which provider owns this domain' from loose fields via a separate fallback helper and a two-field subset signature; the repair must re-centralize that decision on the record, and the resolve-once-and-use behavior is specific to this flow.

rubrics.criterion: Startup per-domain validation (multi-provider mode) judges whole domain entries: the per-entry validation receives the domain record plus whatever surrounding config it needs, and no helper on that validation path re-declares the name/subdomain-list/provider field trio as separate parameters.
rubrics.rationale: The injection rewrote the domain-validation loop in the settings-checking path into a field-taking helper; validation being record-centric again is the second family of carrier signatures this case must resolve.

rubrics.criterion: The manager's per-domain fan-out hands each configured domain entry to the update flow as one value on both execution paths — the background update loop and the synchronous RunOnce path — without destructuring the entry into name/subdomain/provider locals first.
rubrics.rationale: The orchestrating run loop is the origin site where record entries dissolve into loose locals before handoff; un-destructuring the fan-out is required for the record abstraction to reach the update flow at all.

rubrics.criterion: Every caller along the update path was updated consistently with the record-based signatures, including the update success notification, which still reports the provider that handled the update (the domain's own provider, or the global provider when the domain does not name one).
rubrics.rationale: The notification previously derived its '(via <provider>)' provenance from the loose provider field and its fallback; a complete repair wires provenance back from the record-based provider resolution, otherwise callers and notification content silently diverge.

rubrics.criterion: The existing loop-lifecycle tests call the update flow through the record-based form (constructing domain records at their call sites) rather than through any field-taking shim preserved for their benefit, keeping their cancellation and concurrent-shutdown assertions intact.
rubrics.rationale: The tests were mechanically adapted to the field-passing form during injection; a real repair naturally re-adapts them rather than keeping a compatibility shim alive, so this distinguishes a coherent refactor from a wrapper workaround.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not keep the loose parameter list alive through an adapter layer: no method on the update path remains that accepts the domain's name, subdomain list, and provider as separate parameters merely to bundle them into a record before delegating (and no equivalent record-copy wrapper re-declaring the same fields beside the record-based path).
rubrics.rationale: A field-taking wrapper that rebuilds the record would re-impose the recurring field trio this task exists to remove; it is the most plausible 'looks repaired, still clumped' outcome specific to this flow.

rubrics.criterion: The single-field provider fallback helper introduced with the field-passing form (converting one empty provider field to the global provider) is removed or fully absorbed into the record-based provider resolution — not left behind as dead, unreferenced code, and not left still consulted anywhere on the update path.
rubrics.rationale: This helper only exists because the provider lost its record context; leaving it orphaned (or still in use) is an obsolete injected artifact specific to this case and a recognizable incompleteness of the refactor.

rubrics.criterion: No orphaned field-form validation helper remains in the settings-checking path: if per-domain validation still uses helpers, they operate on whole domain entries, and any injected helper taking the name/subdomain-list/provider strings (plus config) is removed once its callers are record-based — not merely bypassed.
rubrics.rationale: The injected validation helper is the second created-by-this-diff artifact; keeping it dead in the tree (or calling it from a wrapper) would leave an obsolete injected artifact that a complete repair deletes.

rubrics.criterion: Per-domain provider selection regresses in none of these ways: a domain that names its own provider stops using it; a domain without its own provider stops falling back to the configured global provider; or a domain-named provider is no longer looked up in the configured providers map with the same 'provider not found for domain' failure when absent.
rubrics.rationale: These are the exact selection behaviors the update flow's provider dispatch and startup validation implement in this instance; each is a concrete plausible failure of a signature-flattening repair.

rubrics.criterion: The per-domain loop lifecycle is preserved: loops still perform one update immediately, then update on the configured interval, return promptly when the shared context is cancelled, and concurrent loops still shut down together; RunOnce still performs exactly one synchronous update per domain and fails the run when a domain's update fails.
rubrics.rationale: The changed signatures sit directly on the loop and RunOnce execution paths guarded only by the loop-lifecycle tests and the manager's exit-code contract; a plausible repair breaks these while rewiring the fan-out.

rubrics.criterion: Update economics are preserved: a record whose current IP equals the cached IP still skips the provider update without sending a notification, and the cached IP still advances only after a successful provider update.
rubrics.rationale: IP-change suppression and cache advancement live inside the one-shot entry whose parameters were reworked; skipping updates when a domain record is now passed by value would silently duplicate provider calls or notifications per tick.

rubrics.criterion: Startup validation verdicts are unchanged: empty domain names and empty subdomains are still rejected; a domain entry whose named provider is missing from the providers map is still rejected; a domain entry without its own provider is still accepted whenever a global provider is configured; and the single-provider legacy mode keeps requiring a non-empty global provider.
rubrics.rationale: The validation path was rewritten from record loops to field tuples for this case; each listed verdict is a concrete misconfiguration this repository explicitly guards, and a record-restore could plausibly drop or broaden one of them.
